### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**3** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a4c0034ed828e7b2203bcf120e484c52e3b6088` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `66928c79c09be648ca292d18bf00a3536743f40a` — the merge of head `be98e5872ff9864fe4c4cffebe20588fcf19317d` into base `2a4c0034ed828e7b2203bcf120e484c52e3b6088`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 66928c79c09be648ca292d18bf00a3536743f40a && git checkout 66928c79c09be648ca292d18bf00a3536743f40a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2a4c0034ed828e7b2203bcf120e484c52e3b6088 be98e5872ff9864fe4c4cffebe20588fcf19317d && git checkout -B drift-repro 2a4c0034ed828e7b2203bcf120e484c52e3b6088 && git merge --no-ff be98e5872ff9864fe4c4cffebe20588fcf19317d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2a4c0034ed828e7b2203bcf120e484c52e3b6088
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `be98e5872ff9864fe4c4cffebe20588fcf19317d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/objectql-strategy.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/__tests__/preview-time-filter-fk-parity.test.ts + packages/services/service-analytics/src/index.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/package.json (`exports`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/preview-group-column-door.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts (`withDeclaredGranularityDefaults`, the preview door call, `generateSql`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/strategies/native-sql-strategy.ts (`canHandle`), packages/services/service-analytics/src/order-key-door.ts (`projectedDimensions`), packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts, packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts (`timeDimensions`, cube `granularities`), packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts (`DatasetSelectionSchema.dateGranularity`)

Inputs: card #28799 (body, triage, claim, os-dev-report `6565320589`), PR #28837 (body, file list, net diff against merge-base `3e05ed1e` with `main`), the check-runs on the head. Every cited file is byte-identical between the merge-base and `origin/main` (`2a4c0034`), so the live tree is the one read. The narrowing face has no `hits`; the floor is both non-prose paths of the diff. The changeset is read for ②, not reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged against the cited code:

1. **The pair is refused on every face — right.** `granularitiesByDimension` keeps every granularity per dimension as spelled; `aggregateGroupKeys` and `executeCrossObject` push one `{ field, dateGranularity }` key per granularity through `pushGroupKey`, whose `same` test compares `dateGranularity` too, so `month` and `year` over one column are two keys. The engine's `assertAggregatedColumnsAreDistinct` (`aggregate-query-shape-door.ts`, at the entry of `engine.aggregate`) then refuses `INVALID_QUERY` / 400 with `param: 'groupBy'`, `path: groupBy.N.field` (object form, no alias ⇒ `.field`), `fields: [column]`. The native face really declines: `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle` returns `false` for any `timeDimensions` entry with a granularity (`native-sql-strategy.ts` line 645), so the ObjectQL strategy answers it. The preview judges the same keys (`assertPreviewGroupColumnsDistinct` calls `aggregateGroupKeys` over the same cube, before `evaluateAnalyticsQueryOverRows`) and minted its refusal from the engine's message, code, status, httpStatus, object, param, path and fields, so the three faces agree field for field, and the test's `refusedAsLive` asserts exactly that set across all three.
2. **The refused shape is only the pair — right.** Read case by case against the two builders at the head:
   - one bucket per column: `grans = [g]` ⇒ one key, as before;
   - buckets of different columns: distinct `field`s, as before;
   - one dimension asked twice at the same granularity: two identical keys, `pushGroupKey` keeps one ⇒ served as one bucket (the new control test);
   - a dimension that is also its own single time dimension: listed-dimension arm, `grans = [g]` ⇒ one bucketed key, map entry deleted, as before;
   - #28744 (`region`, `zone` over `region`): no granularity ⇒ `grans = []` ⇒ raw `field`, deduplicated by `pushGroupKey`, as before;
   - #28765 two spellings of one column (`closed_at` + `OBJECT.closed_at`): two map entries, two keys, the refusal unchanged;
   - `dimensions: ['closed_at', 'closed_at']` with one bucket: bucket then raw ⇒ refused, as before;
   - entries with no granularity (a `dateRange` window only) are skipped, as before; `withDeclaredGranularityDefaults` fills one entry per grouped dimension, so a filled default never yields two granularities;
   - key order: `dimensions` order, then remaining time dimensions in first-appearance order — unchanged, so every existing `path` position holds.
   `executeCrossObject` pushes `baseDimFields` once per dimension while pushing two keys; unreachable divergence, since the engine refuses before `rebucketCrossObject` runs.
3. **`/analytics/query` carries no half-rendered `sql` for the pair — right.** `execute()` awaits `ctx.executeAggregate` before calling `generateSql`, so the engine refuses first and the echo is never reached on that door.
4. **Public surface: nothing widened — right.** `src/index.ts` is untouched (it exports `ObjectQLStrategy`, `NativeSQLStrategy`, the service, plugin, registry, compiler and types, never the module-level builders); `package.json` `exports` has the single `.` entry, so `strategies/objectql-strategy` is not a published subpath. `granularitiesByDimension` is module-private. `AggregateGroupKey`, `aggregateGroupKeys` and `aggregateObjectOf` were already module exports at the merge-base (the preview door imports them on `main`). The only type change is the private method's local `GroupByItem` alias replaced by the existing `AggregateGroupKey`. No new public member on `ObjectQLStrategy`, no new error code or status.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/28799-two-granularities-one-dimension-refused.md`: `'@objectstack/service-analytics': patch`, summary `fix(service-analytics)!:`, `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` line-initial in both the changeset and the PR body, exactly one `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` marker, the remedy stated. `Check Changeset` is green.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. No `packages/spec` file moves; `timeDimensions[]` still parses every entry it parsed before; `DatasetSelectionSchema` is a request contract reading `AnalyticsQuerySchema.shape`, not metadata an author stores; the pair was never a declared value (see ④). Under ruling A, `none` takes `patch`, and the BREAKING carriers (banner, `!`, the arm) stay on it — present.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` matches what the diff publishes: an accept-set narrowing of `queryDataset` and `query` on `@objectstack/service-analytics`, nothing widened. Level `patch` matches. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions: []` — nothing owed.
- Dev flag (out_of_scope_findings): `ObjectQLStrategy.generateSql` (the `/analytics/sql` dry run) still builds its GROUP BY from its own one-granularity `granByDim`, so for the pair it renders one `year` bucket for a statement `execute()` now refuses. Read in the tree at the head: confirmed (lines 691–693, 775, 792). **Judged should-fix as a follow-up card, not a must-fix**, because: (a) the card's three faces are `queryDataset`'s native, ObjectQL and preview; the dry run is a fourth door, outside the order's file surface; (b) the echo runs no engine, so refusing there is a new refusal of its own (keys built via `aggregateGroupKeys` and judged as the preview door judges them), which the order's no-new-gate line reads against; (c) the drift class pre-exists on `main`: for #28765's `dimensions: ['closed_at']` + `timeDimensions: [{ OBJECT.closed_at, month }]` the echo already renders `col AS "closed_at"` beside `bucket AS "OBJECT.closed_at"`, a statement `execute()` refuses — the pair adds one member to that class; (d) `/analytics/query` is unaffected (①.3). But the file's own invariant — `/analytics/sql` and `execute()` accept/reject the SAME set (the #3654 / #10759 comments in `generateSql`) — now has one more exception, so it is owed a card: the echo refuses the same keys, or declares it does not. The seat files it; nothing blocks this PR on it.
- Premise: measured true on `1e019240` on every face (the dev's table). The triage said re-grade to p2 if the live faces really serve a dropped bucket without a word — they did; the re-grade is the seat's, no bearing on the verdict.
- Deviations (one rebase before the gates; the branch recreated after #28794 merged): no bearing; the rebase touched no `service-analytics` file and the ablations are reported at the pre-rebase sha.
- Read observation, not a finding: a host that supplies its own `AnalyticsServiceConfig.executeAggregate` bridge not backed by `engine.aggregate` meets no duplicate-column door and would receive two keys over one column; that premise is #28765's and the preview door's already, unchanged here.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`:

- `packages/spec/src/data/analytics.zod.ts`: a `timeDimensions` entry is `{ dimension, granularity?, dateRange? }` — the schema's own words at the alias table, "a query's time dimension takes exactly one `granularity`". A cube dimension's `granularities` is a default list: "a granularity the query states always wins" — one. `packages/spec/src/api/analytics.zod.ts` `dateGranularity`: "Precedence, per dimension: an explicit `timeDimensions` entry for that dimension wins". `AnalyticsResult` rows are keyed by dimension name and `projectedDimensions` projects a dimension once. At no layer does the spec declare two buckets of one dimension under one name, and there is no answer shape that could carry them.
- `packages/objectql/src/aggregate-query-shape-door.ts` (#25818) lists `groupBy: [{ opened_on, month }, { opened_on, year }]` in its own measured table as a shape the engine refuses `INVALID_QUERY` at `engine.aggregate`. That refusal is published engine behaviour. The strategy's `Map.set` hid it from every face by handing the engine the last entry only.
- So the PR takes no declared capability away at the consumer: it stops the consumer from hiding the engine's refusal, and the refusal that reaches the caller is the engine's, unchanged, with the preview's copy byte-identical. That is the spec's own refusal made real, and it matches Prime Directive 12 (surface loudly, no silent tolerance). Serving both buckets instead would need a new answer shape (an alias on a time dimension) and new spec: a widening, outside the card, and the seat's ruling refused it. A schema-level refinement refusing the pair at parse time would be a `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` change of its own and is not owed here; the engine's refusal names the position already.
- Tried to break it: every selection in ①.2, both key orders, both spellings, beside a raw dimension, beside another dimension, beside a cross-object dimension, and the dry-run door; the only drift found is ③'s echo, pre-existing in class. The tests pin the pair in both orders, both spellings, beside `closed_at`, `region` and `account.name` (both live faces), and the same-granularity control, comparing the three refusals field for field; red-first on base and four ablations are reported.

Must-fix: none. Should-fix: the `generateSql` echo (③), as a follow-up card.

Check-runs on the head: every check-run completed; 35 `success` (Build Core, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates and its seven Lint families, Test Core 1–8, Test UI, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Type Check workspace/source/consumer/debt and TypeScript Type Check, PR-body guards, Check PR Size, Auto Label, Flag docs, Plan Test Core shards, filter), 13 `skipped` by path filter (UI build/lint/type, docs build, Temporal Conformance, opt-in harnesses, the schedule gate), 0 failure, 0 pending. The derived gate families answered green here; nothing was run locally.

**VERDICT: PASS**
